newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SPHINX TO SELL TILES DIVISION.
newsitem.headline: SPHINX TO SELL TILES DIVISION.

text.p: Ceramics and bathroom equipment firm NV Koninklijke Sphinx Gustavsberg said on Tuesday it had reached agreement to sell its tiles division to two venture capital firms and the unit's management.
Sphinx Tiles BV has been sold to ABN AMRO Participaties BV, a unit of ABN AMRO Bank , unlisted Gilde Buy-Out Fund BV and the subsidiary's management.
The deal, of which no financial details were disclosed, is effective from April 1, 1997.
"The sale agreement will be effective from that date, so that the full operational activities will be for the account and risk of the buyers," Sphinx said in a statement.
Sphinx had previously announced it wanted to shed its tiles activities as part of a strategic reorientation of the group.
Sphinx spokesman Johan Boheman told Reuters the tiles unit had annual turnover of 100 million guilders and posted positive results although these were not substantial.
The subsidiary was part of Sphinx's special products group, which originally had annual sales of about 300 million guilders.
It had already sold German unit Schock Bad with annual sales of 50 million guilders from this division to Burgbad .

Boheman said Sphinx was still looking at possible candidates to buy the remainder of the special products division, which now has some 100 million guilders of turnover left. No near-term decisions were expected, he added.
Boheman said Sphinx reiterated its previous forecast that it expected a 15 million guilder loss from ordinary operations in the financial year to March 31, 1997.
An additional 30 million guilder extraordinary charge has been taken to restructure the group's ceramic sanitary ware products division.
Last March, Sphinx announced "substantial" job losses in its Belgian production sites and said it would substantially cut production levels at another unit in Germany.
It also planned to contract out about 20 percent of its present production to low-wage countries.
Sphinx previously said the restructuring would help improve operating results, leading to a modest profit in 1997/98.
The company will announce its results for 1996/97 on June 4.
